scan.summary: This is the company's own yearly summary of work-related injuries and illnesses at the Portland facility for 2025, filled in on the federal OSHA 300A form and signed by the Plant Manager on February 1, 2026 (page 1). It shows 3 recordable injuries: 1 with 6 days away from work and 2 other recordable cases. There were no deaths and no job-transfer or restriction cases. It is a record, so it was checked for completeness and for whether it fits with what the company has already confirmed. It was not checked against a program standard.
scan.freshness_note: This is the latest summary that should exist today. The 2026 summary is not due until February 1, 2027. The 2025 posting period (February 1 – April 30, 2026) and the electronic filing deadline (March 2, 2026) have both passed. Keep this form until at least December 31, 2030.

gaps.title: Annual average employee count does not match the confirmed headcount
gaps.description: The form reports an annual average of 65 employees and 128,400 hours worked in 2025. The company has confirmed 42 employees at Portland. 128,400 hours works out to about 1,975 hours per person for 65 people, which is plausible. For 42 people it would be about 3,057 hours each, which is not. So either headcount dropped after 2025, the figure counts temporary or leased workers, or one of the numbers is wrong. The 2025 average also affects whether the 20-employee threshold for electronic filing applies to the site.
gaps.fix: Check the 2025 payroll and any temp or staffing-agency records to confirm the average and the hours. If the 300A is wrong, correct it and resubmit through OSHA's Injury Tracking Application. If it is right, note that 42 is today's headcount and not the 2025 average.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-001-0700 (300A must show annual average employees and total hours worked covered by the OSHA 300 Log)

gaps.title: No proof of electronic filing for 2025
gaps.description: The company is in Oregon, averaged 20 or more employees in 2025, and reports NAICS 424690. That very likely means this summary had to be filed electronically through OSHA's Injury Tracking Application by March 2, 2026. The files the company holds include no filing receipt. I believe NAICS 4246 is on the designated-industry list (Table 7), but I did not check the table itself.
gaps.fix: Log into OSHA's Injury Tracking Application (osha.gov/injuryreporting) and confirm the 2025 300A was filed. Keep the confirmation. If it was not filed, file it now.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-001-0700(24)(b) and Table 7 (mirrors 29 CFR 1904.41); due March 2 of the following year

gaps.title: Industry code may not match the company's profile
gaps.description: The form lists NAICS 424690, a chemical wholesaler code. The company's profile says chemical manufacturing. The NAICS code decides which designated-industry list the site falls under for electronic filing.
gaps.fix: Confirm the right NAICS code for the Portland establishment, for example against the Oregon unemployment insurance registration, and use it the same way on the 300A and in the Injury Tracking Application.
gaps.citation: OAR 437-001-0700(24) Tables 7 and 8 (designated industries by NAICS)
gaps.quote: Industry description: Chemical and allied products merchant wholesaler; repackaging of acids, caustics and solvents

scan.confidence_notes: The page is clear, and every field, number and signature was read directly from page 1. The case counts add up: the 3 injuries match the 1 days-away case plus the 2 other recordable cases. The Plant Manager signed it, which is usually acceptable as the highest-ranking official at the site. That the electronic filing rule applies is my inference: it rests on the 65-employee average and on my belief that NAICS 4246 is on Oregon's Table 7, which I did not check against the table itself. I cannot tell from this form alone whether the 65 or the 42 is correct. Reporting the 2025 posting period as ended assumes the form was actually posted, which the form cannot show.

All establishments covered by Part 1904 must complete this Summary page, even if no work-related injuries or illnesses occurred during the year. Remember to review the Log to verify that
the entries are complete and accurate before completing this summary. Using the Log, count the individual entries you made for each category. Then write the totals below, making sure
you've added the entries from every page of the Log. If you had no cases, write "0." Employees, former employees, and their representatives have the right to review the OSHA Form 300 in
